tiktok.author: filthierdemonrat
tiktok.body:
Surely them suggesting that you borrow well into the hundreds is just a suggestion right?
On my for you page, I've been seeing ads for apps that do cash advances. And I know the word I'm about to use has been thrown around, misused and abused, especially with these last couple discourses. But these ads and the respective apps are predatory because they will always have some little skit where the person getting the cash advance. They're short for gas, they're short for groceries, and they're waiting on their next paycheck. They tend to really hone in on the fact that the person is waiting on their next paycheck. So obviously these are aimed at low income/working class people. And there are a lot of reasons to not do a cash advance, but the main reason is that it will put you in a loop of debt because you have to pay that money back. Now you might be thinking, well, duh, Devin, it's not free money. But here's the thing, it comes across as if it is. Like, come on the whole, it's quick and it's easy. No credit check, no late fee. The people behind these apps, they know that their users are in a distressing position, so they're gonna be more concerned with keeping their head above water and not the future consequences. The intended targets of these apps are already having to decide between food or paying the bills, and they gets little cash advance. The next paycheck comes, and guess what? They're in an even worse position now. They have to decide between food bills or paying back these people
